thread:
incident-bot: Pager: private-vpc cluster east-5 - GPU serving queue length >95% for 6m. Autoscaler attempted 4 scale actions, 3 failed. Rollups: request_backlog=1820, avg_token_latency=1.8s, error_rate=12%. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/svcs/autoscale-private|autoscale-private>.
amber: Acked. I'm oncall. Starting triage — assigning to @joel (sre) for infra check, @alex (eng-runtime) for routing/fallback, @lyn (platform) to check cloud provider/quotas.
joel: On it. Looking at cluster east-5 now.
joel: K8s events show node provisioning stuck in Pending with reason ProvisionerFailure and cloud-provider errors showing: `QuotaExceeded: RequestedInstanceTypeLimitExceeded` and `NoCapacity: We currently do not have sufficient capacity in AZ eu-central-1a for type p4`
amber: That matches the autoscaler logs I pulled: `scale_attempt id=3745 -> failed: node_request_rejected: capacity_error`. Do we have a node pool max or quota hit?
lyn: Confirmed there's a nodepool cap at 60 for that tenant. Usage is 59 and autoscaler tried to add 4. Also seeing cloud provider throttle 429s on instance create API from provisioning service. I just opened a support case with provider (case #CP-98233). ETA from provider agent ~35m.
alex: Routing note: fallback to hosted is configured for this tenant but is limited to 30% by policy. We can temporarily increase to 60% to shed load from private cluster while we remediate. Would need a manual policy change.
amber: Do we have permission to bump the fallback? Is there an automated safe-route?
alex: I can apply a temporary routing override: `PATCH /v1/routing/tenants/{tid} {"private_fallback_threshold":0.6}` — will take ~2m and will start shifting new requests to hosted capacity. It will also change cost profile, pinging finance but prefer availability.
amber: Do it. Please also enable model-variant downgrade for long-running requests (route to rxx-small-quant when latency > 800ms).
alex: Applying override now. Pushing change... `200 OK` — override active. Traffic shifting starting. Expect queue to drop in ~90s.
bill: From customer ops: Customer AcmeAnalytics is showing 503s on their ML endpoints. They just reported that their scheduled nightly batch started and it's hitting queueing. Impact: 1 large customer degraded, others may be affected if we don't recover.
joel: OK focusing on node provisioning failure. Two issues: 1) tenant node pool cap (60) prevented autoscaler from increasing; 2) cloud provider regional capacity causing instance creation retries and throttle. Immediate mitigations: - increase tenant nodepool cap to 90 (manual override) - request burst capacity from cloud provider support - temporarily enable fallback routing (done) - manual scale via reserved nodes on other AZs if allowed
amber: Can you increase nodepool cap? Who owns that config?
lyn: I can update tenant config to bump cap to 90. Making change now and will trigger autoscaler again. Note: bumping the cap does not bypass cloud provider capacity issues but removes our internal limiter.
lyn: Updated tenant nodepool cap to 90. Patching autoscaler to re-evaluate.
joel: Re-triggering scale: autoscaler now requests 6 nodes. Cloud provider still returning intermittent `NoCapacity` for p4 in eu-central-1a but eu-central-1b has capacity for lower-spec `a10` instances. We can change requested instance type to `a10` as a temporary fallback, or mix.
amalex: (typo) — alex: We can accept mixed instance types — runtime supports model-to-node matching. If we provision a10 nodes we should also decrease max batch size for those model shards to avoid OOM. I'll update the serving profile to conservative batch size on those nodes.
joel: Provisioning call partially succeeds: 4 a10 nodes created in eu-central-1b, 2 p4 pending in 1a. New nodes are joining, kubelets Ready for the 4 a10.
incident-bot: System note: routing override in place for tenant tid-04x; fallback threshold 60% active.
bill: Customers seeing partial recovery, AcmeAnalytics reports reduced errors from 503 -> 200 with higher latencies. Thanks.
amber: Good. We need to confirm no further churn. Watching queue.
(3m pass)
joel: Queue length dropping from 1800 -> 420. Token latency down to 700ms. Error rate falling to 3%. Autoscaler reports scale success for the 4 a10 nodes. P4 nodes still pending due to AZ capacity.
lyn: Cloud provider updated case: CP-98233 - they've scheduled capacity rebalancing and expect p4 availability back in ~40m. They also said there were elevated API rate limits causing slower provisioning; working to lift those.
alex: Serving adjustments applied: per-node batch size reduced by 35% on a10 nodes, runtime will preferentially pack smaller-req models on those nodes. No QoS regressions observed in warm tests.
amber: Next steps: - keep routing override until p4 capacity returns or we confirm steady state - follow up with provider for capacity ETA - post-incident: evaluate increasing fallback thresholds for tenant auto when private cluster under pressure - update runbook to include nodepool_cap check earlier
joel: I'll create a short incident doc and link to this thread. Assigning follow-ups: @lyn to drive provider ticket to resolution, @alex to validate serving perf on a10 for next 48h, @amber to own postmortem and customer comms.
lyn: Provider escalated, asked for our expected ramp timeline; I shared our traffic curve for the night. They asked for 15m more to verify.
bill: I'll send a quick note to AcmeAnalytics letting them know we've applied fallback and are provisioning extra nodes; estimated full recovery in under 1h.
amber: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. @joel — are you taking follow-up oncall?
joel: I can take handoff for the next 2 hours. Amber, please add me to the incident doc when you create it.
amber: Incident update will be in #incidents and I will link to the doc. Closing pager for now as immediate customer-impact reduced, but marking P1->P2 while we watch and await p4 capacity. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Pager resolved (ack closed) by amber at 2159878903.
amber: Quick timeline for PM: root cause — combination of tenant nodepool cap + cloud provider AZ capacity shortfall + provider API throttling causing slow node provisioning. Immediate mitigations: routing override, mixed-instance provisioning, manual cap bump. Proposed postmortem items: add automated early detection for nodepool cap, refine fallback thresholds, run periodic capacity checks with provider.
alex: Adding note: runtime needs a quick-mode to auto-reduce batch sizes when running on mixed-instance pools; I'll prototype a toggled flag.
joel: I'll attach kube event logs and autoscaler logs to the doc.
bill: Customer communicated, they acknowledged and will monitor.
amber: Thanks all. Will open formal postmortem and schedule follow-up meeting.
